findings.statement: Management has schedule, cost and reputational incentives that favour approval while also controlling the safety decision.
Engineering dissent exists and a senior representative proposes waiting, yet management can reverse the no-go recommendation.
Delay and escalation are less irreversible exercises of power than authorizing the mission now.

principle_assessments.reason: Approval now uses irreversible authority when reversible alternatives can address the same mission objective.
The conflict between safety responsibility and schedule pressure plus unresolved dissent requires independent or higher-level scrutiny.
The process must preserve the practical force of engineering challenge rather than treating management authority as decisive evidence.

information_requests: What independent escalation route exists when contractor management reverses engineering no-go advice?
alternatives_or_safeguards: Escalate dissent; delay; require explicit safety-signoff based on evidence rather than schedule need.
evidence_that_could_change_view: Independent technical review resolving the material uncertainty in favour of safety.
